papers.title: Addressable Control of Hybrid Spin Qubit in Single-Atom Copper-Modified Fullerene
papers.authors: Bingcai Chen, Jiahao Chen, Pengxiang Fu, Di Zhang, Hao Li, Jiayue Yuan, Jianyu Liu, Dahui Zhao, Tian Jiang, Gao-Lei Hou, Shanshan Wang, Shen Zhou
papers.summary: Copper centers dispersed in a magnetically quiet fullerene matrix support coherent electron and nuclear spin manipulation. Dynamical decoupling extends electron coherence, while quadrupolar splitting enables selective access to nuclear levels and hyperfine coupling accelerates nuclear rotations.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Directly relevant to chemically engineered hybrid spin registers, electron-nuclear addressability, and coherence-preserving molecular host design.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine coherent manipulation and addressability in molecularly constructed electron-spin platforms.

papers.title: Periodic Trends in Radical-Mediated Exchange Coupling and Magnetic Anisotropy in Ln2N2 Complexes
papers.authors: Md. Ashraful Islam, Nicholas F. Chilton
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.summary: Multiconfigurational calculations compare radical-bridged lanthanide dimers across the series, separating crystal-field anisotropy from exchange interactions. The analysis identifies dominant virtual electron-transfer contributions in the gadolinium analogue and describes how exchange varies despite a broadly similar crystal-field potential.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Provides a molecular-level framework for interpreting radical-mediated exchange and anisotropy; this is a computational magnetism study, not a qubit-coherence demonstration.

relatedPapers.reason: Connects radical-based molecular architectures with the control of magnetic interactions.

papers.title: Phonon-Bottlenecked Spin Relaxation of Er 3 + : CaWO 4 at MilliKelvin Temperatures
papers.authors: S. Rajendran, B. Mistri, P. K. Sharma, S. E. Kubatkin, A. V. Danilov, S. Dhomkar, S. E. de Graaf, V. Ranjan
papers.versionEvidence: Matching title and author list in publisher metadata and arXiv record
papers.summary: Electron-spin relaxation in erbium-doped calcium tungstate is measured through coupling to a superconducting resonator at millikelvin temperatures. Excitation-dependent relaxation and its temperature dependence support a phonon-bottleneck interpretation, highlighting limitations on relaxation in rare-earth spin ensembles.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Provides an experimental comparison for identifying phonon-related relaxation mechanisms and excitation-dependent effects in spin materials.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate unusual spin-lattice relaxation and the role of the phonon environment.

papers.title: Optimal Calibration of Qubit Detuning and Crosstalk
papers.authors: David Shnaiderov, Matan Ben Dov, Yoav Woldiger, Assaf Hamo, Eugene Demler, Emanuele G. Dalla Torre
papers.summary: Ramsey protocols are optimized using Fisher information to estimate qubit detuning and crosstalk. Theory and experiments with an NV center and superconducting transmons favor measuring two quadratures at one time, reducing calibration effort while preserving parameter accuracy.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Calibration strategies can help distinguish control imperfections from intrinsic coherence loss in spin experiments.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address measurement reliability in the presence of imperfect qubit control.

papers.title: Quantum transport in disordered spin networks: Emergent timescales and competing pathways
papers.authors: Roi Nevo, Brett Min, Maggie Lawrence, Dvira Segal, Nir Bar-Gill
papers.summary: A dissipative model of a spin impurity coupled to a small disordered spin network develops widely separated relaxation timescales. Simulations and a minimal three-site model attribute slow transfer to hierarchical couplings and effective detuning generated by strongly hybridized clusters.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Helps assess whether heterogeneous spin networks can produce slow relaxation without assuming a single homogeneous bath.

relatedPapers.reason: Connects microscopic open-system dynamics with the interpretation of measured relaxation rates.

papers.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
papers.summary: Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations predict that vacancy aggregation can lengthen NV Hahn-echo coherence at fixed paramagnetic spin density. Direction-dependent transition frequencies suppress resonant bath-spin exchange, challenging the assumption that all vacancy complexes necessarily worsen coherence.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Offers a concrete bath-dynamics mechanism to examine when interpreting coherence changes after defect processing; the result is theoretical.

relatedPapers.reason: Complements reliable echo characterization by examining the microscopic bath dynamics behind coherence decay.

papers.title: Multilayer Multistate Reaction Coordinate Model for Nonadiabatic Dynamics in Open Quantum Systems
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.summary: A hierarchical reaction-coordinate transformation maps multistate harmonic environments into chains of collective modes. Benchmarks include spin-boson and molecular charge-transfer models; truncated chains reproduce the tested dynamics with fewer degrees of freedom while exposing relationships between nuclear motion and electronic populations.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Offers a computational route for reducing structured environments in models of molecular spin and charge dynamics; accuracy must be checked for each truncation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use explicit environment models to study dynamics beyond simple perturbative relaxation descriptions.

papers.title: Low-field dephasing time of an optically polarized NV$^-$ spin bath beyond the P1 limit in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion and exact spin-bath study
papers.summary: Spin-bath simulations compare optically polarized NV ensembles with substitutional-nitrogen baths at equal density. They predict longer dephasing times at low fields, while off-axis moments erode the advantage at higher fields and bath relaxation limits Hahn-echo gains.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Provides field-dependent design guidance for ensemble spin sensing; the predicted gains are simulations, not new experimental sensitivity measurements.

relatedPapers.reason: Complements sensing-sequence design by examining the bath-limited coherence available to a sensor.

papers.title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of a Tb(III)-MOF and Its Luminescent Sensing for Erythromycin, Tetracycline, and 3,5-Dinitrosalicylic Acid
papers.authors: Rui Dai, Xinyue Guo, Chunxue Zhou, Yue She, Zhiguo Kong, Xuecheng Chen
papers.summary: A terbium MOF detects three aqueous analytes through luminescence quenching and is incorporated into test strips. Time-resolved emission and XPS indicate analyte-dependent pathways, including collision quenching, competitive absorption, electron transfer, and interactions involving defect sites.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Useful for comparing chemical selectivity and competing readout mechanisms in porous sensors; the readout is luminescent rather than spin-quantum sensing.

relatedPapers.reason: Both couple analyte recognition in a porous framework to a measurable response, using different readout mechanisms.

papers.title: Innovative Zinc(II) Metal−Organic Frameworks Featuring Pyridine-Sulfonate-Imine Linkers for Microextraction of Plasticizers and Selective Luminescent Detection of Toxic Oxyanions
papers.authors: Azadeh Mirzaahmadi, Sakha Pezhhanfar, Seyed Abolfazl Hosseini-Yazdi, Mir Ali Farajzadeh, Mahdi Khodaparast Aval, Morgane Poupon, Erika Samolova, Michal Dušek, Seyyed Morteza Seyyed Alavi
papers.summary: Diffusion crystallization produces two zinc coordination frameworks with distinct channel architectures. One framework supports extraction of plastic additives and selective aqueous luminescence quenching by dichromate and permanganate, linking pore structure with adsorption and chemical detection.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Provides a comparison of recognition, pore accessibility, and optical sensing in frameworks without implying demonstrated quantum sensing.

relatedPapers.reason: Relates framework-defined analyte environments to sensing selectivity through a complementary optical approach.

papers.title: Switching of Exciton-Polaritons in Covalent Organic Framework-Based Optical Resonators through Interaction with the Molecular Environment
papers.authors: Beatriz de Sola-Báez, Tigmansu Pal, Diego M. Juela, Laura Caliò, Mauricio E. Calvo, Juan F. Galisteo-López, Jesús Hernández-Saz, Miriam Herrera, Bettina V. Lotsch, Hernán Míguez
papers.summary: COF nanoplate films integrated into optical cavities exhibit exciton-polariton formation. Water-vapor adsorption changes optical absorption and reversibly switches the resonators between strong and weak coupling, demonstrating a porous-material route to guest-responsive photonic devices.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Connects molecular guests, framework optical properties, and device operation, offering a useful comparison for optically active molecular materials.

relatedPapers.reason: Both motivate optical functionality in framework-based quantum-material platforms, with distinct physical mechanisms.

papers.title: Ionic-liquid-assisted room-temperature dry etching of metal–organic frameworks
papers.authors: Yumeng Zheng, Momoka Muraoka, Koki Egawa, Kentaro Kinoshita
papers.summary: Ionic-liquid infiltration stabilizes beam-sensitive MOFs during room-temperature ion-beam processing. The study demonstrates fine patterning below 100 nm and examines how ionic-liquid choice affects damage, with possible mechanisms involving copper reduction and cleavage of metal-oxygen bonds.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Directly informs fabrication strategies for fragile MOF devices and the need to separate processing-induced damage from intrinsic material behavior.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address processing constraints and device fabrication in sensitive metal-organic frameworks.

papers.title: Coherent Spin-Photon Interface of Single PL6 Oxygen Vacancy Centers in 4H-SiC
papers.authors: Zhen-Xuan He, Gergő Thiering, Xiangru Han, Rui-Jian Liang, Ji-Yang Zhou, Shuo Ren, Wu-Xi Lin, Zhi-He Hao, Qi-Cheng Hu, Jun-Feng Wang, Adam Gali, Jin-Shi Xu, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo
papers.summary: Spectroscopy and first-principles calculations examine single PL6 oxygen-vacancy centers in silicon carbide. Oxygen-modified excited states produce spin-selective intersystem crossing; resonant measurements demonstrate initialization, coherent optical and spin control, and millisecond coherence.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Offers a solid-state comparison for linking electronic structure, optical readout, and spin coherence when designing molecular spin-photon interfaces.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern optically addressable spin platforms relevant to quantum-memory interfaces.

papers.title: Stimuli-Responsive Viologen-Based Coordination Supramolecular Isomers Modulated by π-Stacking Interactions
papers.authors: Xu-Dong Yang, Jing Zhang, Zhonghang Chen, Shi-Li Li, Xian-Ming Zhang
papers.summary: Two viologen-based copper coordination isomers exhibit different packing arrangements despite shared composition. Crystallography links a pi-stacked framework and a denser chain architecture to contrasting photochromic, thermochromic, and photothermal responses, emphasizing intermolecular interactions as a design variable.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Provides a concrete structure-property comparison for controlling packing and stimulus response in molecular framework materials.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how molecular interactions and packing arrangements influence material properties.

papers.title: Mechanochemical Synthesis and Co‐Former–Controlled Assembly of Azobenzene Polycarboxylate Organic Salts: From Framework Node to Passive Guest in HOF‐Like Architectures
papers.authors: Ashutosh Shrivastava, Jyotishka Nath, Madison Rader, Mihaela C. Stefan, Michael C. Biewer
papers.summary: Mechanochemical grinding followed by recrystallization produces two azobenzene-based organic salts. Changing an imidazole co-former to its methylated analogue switches its structural role from network node to pore guest, yielding different hydrogen-bonded architectures verified by single-crystal diffraction.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Illustrates how small chemical changes redirect framework assembly; these are hydrogen-bonded organic salts rather than demonstrated porous quantum devices.

relatedPapers.reason: Offers a complementary synthesis example connecting molecular chemistry with crystalline assembly.

papers.title: Continuous Increase in the Framework Flexibility of ZIF-90 with Crystal-Size Reduction to the Nanoscale: Evidence for Missing Metal Nodes Using Single-Crystal Infrared Spectroscopy
papers.authors: Akalanka B. Ekanayake, Collin S. Hill, Thumini R. Dias, Leonard R. MacGillivray, Alexei V. Tivanski
papers.summary: Single-crystal mechanical and spectroscopic measurements reveal increasing flexibility as ZIF-90 crystals shrink. The size dependence correlates with missing-metal-node defects, linking nanoscale crystal dimensions, defect populations, and elastic behavior through a measured power-law relationship.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Relevant to separating crystal-size and defect effects when comparing framework synthesis batches; retained as an older, previously unpushed discovery.

relatedPapers.reason: Both motivate careful control and characterization of framework crystal size and quality.
